text:
Aisha (sre): Heads-up — our blackbox canary in us-west1 started showing a pattern where streaming handshakes succeed but token emission stalls ~25-35s into the stream. Not a total failure (websocket stays open) but clients see a long silence then a burst. Started ~2026-03-17 18:02 UTC.
Tom (eng-runtime): Ugh. Do we have probe output + raw logs? Could be KV-cache misses or a kernel scheduling stall.
Aisha (sre): I grabbed the probe dump — attaching inline snippet. Note the sequence: initial HEADERS, 101 upgrade, then some keepalive frames, then at t=26s there are repeated TLS retransmits in the pod logs and then a big gap.

# probe excerpt
```
[00:00] CONNECT -> 101 Switching Protocols
[00:01] STREAM_START (req id=abc123)
[00:26] keepalive ping
[00:27] TLS_RETRANS x5
[00:28] no tokens emitted for 27s
[00:55] tokens resume (burst of 400 tokens)
```

Lin (eng-ml): That pattern screams TCP/TLS-level retransmits causing the stream to stall. Could also be host NIC interrupt storms or kernel soft-lockups when GPU DMA stalls. Any correlation with node GPU mem pressure?
Aisha (sre): Checked prometheus for node_gpu_util and gpu_mem_free -> there are short spikes around the same times (see below). Spikes coincide with multiple pods on the same node hitting >92% GPU memory (OOM evictions not happening but high pressure).

Prom query I used:
```
max_over_time(nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes - nvidia_gpu_memory_free_bytes[1m])
```

Tom (eng-runtime): Two parallel items: 1) we should improve the blackbox probe to surface 'warm vs cold' behavior (KV cache warmup causes different network/compute patterns), 2) tune alerting so transient single-probe flaps don't wake paging. Proposal: create a composite alert that fires only when both streaming-silence ratio > 5% over 5m AND p99_stream_latency > 5s. Example prom rule: 

```
- alert: StreamingProbeTailLatency
  expr: |
    (sum(rate(probe_stream_silence_seconds_count[5m])) by (region) / sum(rate(probe_stream_total[5m])) by (region)) > 0.05
    and histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(probe_stream_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region)) > 5
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Streaming probe tail latency high in {{ $labels.region }}"
```

Evan (platform): Also cost note — our streaming probes are expensive (open socket time + token bursts). Suggest sampling at 10% for broad coverage but keep a small set (fixed canaries) at 100% in each region. For embeddings checks we can downsample to 0.5-1% because they are cheaper. We should add a Grafana panel showing probe cost burn: tokens_emitted * token_cost per probe_id.
Lin (eng-ml): For root cause: add a 'warmup check' to the probe flow. Steps: 1) send short prompt to warm KV cache, 2) wait 200-500ms, 3) send the actual streaming prompt and measure first-byte latency + inter-token gaps, 4) repeat after forcing a cold start (restart model worker) to compare. This will let us separate network/TLS stalls from cold-model initialization.
Aisha (sre): I pushed a temporary variant of the probe that implements the warmup flow to the canary group in us-west1. OpsBot reports 120 runs so far: 6 runs showed the stall pattern (5%), matching the observed error ratio.

OpsBot: [auto] probe.us-west1.kv-warmup canary ran 120 checks in last 30m, 6 checks flagged tail-stall, avg tokens/req=312, est token-cost=$0.065

Tom (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) Evan, add cost panel + mark fixed canaries (10% vs 100%). 2) Lin, collect paired warm/cold traces from the canary and dump GPU counters for the node during stalls. 3) Aisha, update the composite alert rule above and create a muted window for non-working-hours to reduce noise.
Evan (platform): I'll add the Grafana panels and a cost alert if probe token-cost > $X/hr aggregated.
Aisha (sre): Thanks — I'll keep the canary running and attach full traces if the pattern widens to other regions. For now it's limited to a couple us-west nodes.
Tom (eng-runtime): If we confirm TLS retransmits are the trigger, we should also check NIC driver versions and kernel patches on those nodes before we chase runtime changes.
Lin (eng-ml): Agreed. Also will add a short Tensor core/PCIe stall counter to the node exporter so we have better correlation next time.
Aisha (sre): Closing the loop here: will post an update tomorrow with warm/cold trace diffs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
